# Navigation & Product Title Latency — Codebase Analysis ## 1. Overall project structure Small **Next.js App Router** shop demo (Next `16.3.0-canary.80`, React 19) with **Cache Components** enabled. | Path | Role | |------|------| | `/workspace/package.json` | Next 16 canary + React 19 | | `/workspace/next.config.ts` | `cacheComponents: true` (PPR / static shell + streaming) | | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | Root layout + static metadata (`title: 'Shop'`) | | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | Home | | `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` | Product page (single route, no dynamic segment) | | `/workspace/lib/data.ts` | Dynamic inventory data (`connection()` + random values) | | `/workspace/tsconfig.json` | `@/*` path alias | **No** `loading.tsx`, **no** `Suspense`, **no** parallel routes (`@slot`), **no** skeleton components, **no** client components, **no** CSS files. ```1:7:/workspace/next.config.ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` With `cacheComponents: true`, Next prerenders a **static shell** and streams uncached/runtime work behind Suspense. Anything awaited at the top of the page without a Suspense boundary **blocks** the whole page (including client navigations from Home). --- ## 2. Home → product routing ### Home (`/`) ```1:11:/workspace/app/page.tsx import Link from 'next/link' export default function Home() { return (

Home

Welcome to our store!

View Product
) } ``` - Fully static Server Component (no data fetching). - Client navigation via `next/link` to `/product`. - Prefetch will try to fetch the product route’s RSC payload; that payload is blocked by the same dynamic await (see below). ### Product (`/product`) ```1:13:/workspace/app/product/page.tsx import { getInventory } from '@/lib/data' export default async function ProductPage() { const inventory = await getInventory() return (

Premium Widget

{inventory.count} in stock

Price: ${inventory.price}

) } ``` Routing is file-based App Router only: ``` app/ layout.tsx → wraps all routes page.tsx → / product/ page.tsx → /product ``` No `app/product/[id]`, no nested layouts under product, no `loading.tsx` / `error.tsx` / `template.tsx`. ### Root layout ```1:18:/workspace/app/layout.tsx import type { Metadata } from 'next' export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Shop', description: 'E-commerce product store', } export default function RootLayout({ children, }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) { return ( {children} ) } ``` Layout is static and does not fetch data; it is not the bottleneck. The page segment is. --- ## 3. How the product title is loaded/rendered The title is a **hardcoded static string** in the product page JSX: ```tsx

Premium Widget

``` It does **not** come from `getInventory()` or any async API. Stock count and price do. Yet the title only appears **after** `await getInventory()` finishes, because both live in the **same** async Server Component that awaits inventory first, then returns the full tree. --- ## 4. Data fetching / loading / streaming (what exists today) ### Data layer ```1:9:/workspace/lib/data.ts import { connection } from 'next/server' export async function getInventory() { await connection() return { count: Math.floor(Math.random() * 50), price: (Math.random() * 100).toFixed(2), } } ``` - `connection()` from `next/server` **defers rendering until a real request** (opts out of prerender for that subtree). - Intended for per-request values (`Math.random()` here). - Next docs: with Cache Components, anything that calls `connection()` should sit **inside** a `` boundary so the static shell can still ship. ### Missing streaming/loading patterns | Pattern | Present? | |---------|----------| | `loading.tsx` | No | | `` around inventory | No | | Skeleton / deferred title shell | No | | Parallel routes / `@slot` | No | | `use cache` on product name | No | | Streaming split of title vs inventory | No | So the product page is one blocking async unit: **title + inventory** wait together. --- ## 5. What blocks the title from appearing immediately ### Causal chain 1. User clicks **View Product** on Home (`Link` → `/product`). 2. Client navigates; Next needs the product page RSC payload. 3. `ProductPage` is `async` and **first** runs `await getInventory()`. 4. `getInventory()` calls `await connection()` → waits for request-time (dynamic; not in static shell). 5. Only after that does the component return JSX including `

Premium Widget

`. 6. There is **no** Suspense boundary and **no** `loading.tsx`, so: - Nothing can stream early. - Nothing goes into the static shell for the page body. - With Cache Components, this is a classic **blocking-route** pattern: uncached/runtime work at page root without Suspense. ### Why this is worse with `cacheComponents: true` Docs (`streaming.md`, `08-caching.md`) emphasize: - Static shell = layouts + Suspense **fallbacks** + non-awaited content. - If you `await` dynamic/runtime work at the **top of the page**, everything below is blocked and cannot be in the shell. - Client navigations are also validated for instant shells: wrap dynamic work in Suspense / push it down. Here the title is static but **structurally trapped** behind the inventory await. ### Visual model ``` Current: ProductPage └── await getInventory() ← connection() blocks entire page └──

Premium Widget

← static, but waits

count / price

Desired (Cache Components): ProductPage (sync / no await at top) └──

Premium Widget

← static shell / instant ← streams after connection() ``` --- ## 6. Existing patterns in this codebase / Next 16 docs (fix approaches) There are **no** local skeleton/Suspense examples in app code; the intended patterns come from Next’s Cache Components docs (already in `node_modules/next/dist/docs`). ### Approach A (best fit): Split static title + Suspense inventory Matches docs for “Streaming uncached data” and “Random values and timestamps” (`connection()` + Suspense): ```tsx // Conceptual fix for app/product/page.tsx import { Suspense } from 'react' import { getInventory } from '@/lib/data' async function Inventory() { const inventory = await getInventory() return ( <>

{inventory.count} in stock

Price: ${inventory.price}

) } export default function ProductPage() { return (

Premium Widget

Loading inventory...

}>
) } ``` - Title is in the static shell → appears immediately on navigation. - Inventory stays dynamic (`connection()` + random) and streams when ready. - Aligns with `connection()` docs: wrap the component that calls it in Suspense. ### Approach B: Route-level `loading.tsx` Add `/workspace/app/product/loading.tsx` as an instant fallback for the whole page segment. - Helps: shows *something* immediately (skeleton). - Does **not** show the real title early unless the loading UI hardcodes “Premium Widget”. - Coarser than Approach A; title still not part of the real shell content. ### Approach C: `use cache` on static product info (if title ever becomes data) If product name later comes from a DB/API and is shareable across users: ```tsx async function getProduct() { 'use cache' // return { title: 'Premium Widget', ... } } ``` Inventory would still use `connection()` inside Suspense. Not needed today (title is already a string literal). ### Approach D: Parallel routes e.g. `@inventory` slot — overkill for this fixture; no parallel-route usage exists. ### Not recommended here - Removing `connection()` without caching would break Cache Components rules for `Math.random()` (blocking-prerender-random). - Awaiting inventory at page top and only “hoping” for streaming — without Suspense it will keep blocking. --- ## 7. Summary | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | Framework / routing | Next.js 16 App Router; `/` → `/product` via `Link` | | Product route | `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` (static path) | | Title source | Hardcoded `

Premium Widget

` | | Why title is slow | Same async page awaits `getInventory()` → `connection()` before any JSX | | Loading/Suspense | None present | | Config | `cacheComponents: true` expects static shell + Suspense for dynamic bits | | Likely fix | Don’t await inventory at page root; render title outside; wrap inventory child in `` (optionally add `loading.tsx` as coarser UX) | **Root cause:** structural coupling of a static title to request-time inventory via a single top-level `await`, with no Suspense boundary under Cache Components / PPR. session_id: ses_0bcdad7c3ffehIXIlGhqi2sWIN
